summary: Today’s pulse tracks Russian military plane crashes killing all 19 on board, US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers, and NSA claims temporary internal network outage caused by ‘scheduled routine maintenance’ – live. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are custody, texas, and diego. In the background, Eight-year-old Haitian boy returns home after release from ICE custody and Markwayne Mullin defends private-jet trip to football game as millions hit by flight delays keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Russian military plane crashes killing all 19 on board
headlines.description: Russia's defence ministry says it preliminarily believes a technical malfunction was the cause of the crash in the Kemerovo region.

headlines.title: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
headlines.description: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.

headlines.title: NSA claims temporary internal network outage caused by ‘scheduled routine maintenance’ – live

I’m like hell yeah, because the point for me is Medicare For All. I don’t care who puts their name on it. I need to go back and talk to Michiganders, and I need to know that our service made their lives easier,” he said at the Atlantic Summit in Washington DC.

headlines.title: Eight-year-old Haitian boy returns home after release from ICE custody
headlines.description: Child reunited with family after he was detained by immigration agents in San Diego and transferred to Texas An eight-year-old Haitian boy who was put into restraints and detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November and transferred to a facility in Texas has been reunited with his family in California . Representative Juan Vargas shared a photograph of the boy and his family in a social media post on Monda, writing: “11 days ago, an 8-year-old in San Diego was taken into federal custody during an immigration check-in. He was separated from his loved ones and held in a facility in Texas. Today, he’s finally home.”

headlines.title: Markwayne Mullin defends private-jet trip to football game as millions hit by flight delays
headlines.description: Trump homeland security chief says ‘we still got to live our life’ amid outcry over journey to LSU on government plane US homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin has defended his decision to fly in a private government to a college football game on Saturday as Americans weathered widespread flight delays and cancellations , saying: “We still got to live our life.” Mullin, a former US senator from Oklahoma, traveled on a government aircraft on Saturday to watch a football game between Louisiana State University and the University of Texas, the New York Post reported on Tuesday . The trip to Baton Rouge, Louisiana, came about a day after a four-hour ground stop that led to thousands of flights being delayed or cancelled – and an estimated 1.5 million people were stranded.

headlinePool.title: National Security Agency network for internal communications goes down
headlinePool.description: NSA issues ‘code yellow’ as NSANet, used by staff to share classified material, including top-secret intelligence, fails The National Security Agency said on Tuesday that it had experienced “temporary degradation” during scheduled routine maintenance, after reports that its classified internal communications network had gone down. In a statement, the agency said some internal systems were affected but that “mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational” and its ability to defend national security continues. It said its infrastructure is built with “multiple layers of redundancy” to keep operations running during planned maintenance or unexpected events.

headlinePool.title: “Trump was in bed with Jensen”: Critics balk at Huang’s wish to return to Nvidia
headlinePool.description: “I love our country”: Jensen Huang’s apology comes amid escalating Nvidia probes.

headlinePool.title: University of Birmingham pauses plans to move Shakespeare Institute after outcry
headlinePool.description: Vice-chancellor halts proposed relocation from Stratford-upon-Avon but offers no guarantees over future The University of Birmingham has paused plans to move its much-loved Shakespeare Institute from Stratford-upon-Avon to its city campus after an outcry from scholars, actors and enthusiasts around the world. Prof Adam Tickell, the university’s vice-chancellor and principal, issued a statement on Tuesday evening saying proposals to relocate the institute and its renowned 60,000-volume library to the university’s Edgbaston campus would be put on hold while its future was explored.

headlinePool.title: American soldier held in UK suspected of spying for Russia taken into US military custody
headlinePool.description: Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner was arrested by British police on 10 November over allegations related to espionage A US soldier who was arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia has been taken into custody by the US military, police have said. Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, 41, was detained by British counter-terrorism police ‌on 10 November in Gloucestershire over allegations relating ⁠to espionage.

headlinePool.title: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
headlinePool.description: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.

headlinePool.title: Trump in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents
headlinePool.description: The US president said he would be open to a one-on-one meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin "if it's available".

headlinePool.title: Trump nominates Chris LaNeve as army chief after Hegseth fired predecessor
headlinePool.description: LaNeve, who served as Hegseth’s senior military commander, nominated to permanently replace Gen Randy George Donald Trump has nominated Gen Chris LaNeve to be the US army’s top officer, making permanent his interim service after defense secretary Pete Hegseth unexpectedly fired his predecessor in April. LaNeve had been serving as Hegseth’s senior military commander before his nomination for a fourth star and service as vice chief of staff of the army in February.

headlinePool.title: Palestinian woman shot dead by Israeli settlers near Jericho, witnesses say
headlinePool.description: Bullet hit 72-year-old Fadha Wadha in head outside her home in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, in the West Bank, say residents A 72-year-old Palestinian woman has been shot dead in an overnight attack by Israeli settlers in a village near Jericho where settlers have recently moved in after taking over several Palestinian homes. Fadha Wadha was standing outside her home in al-Duyuk al-Tahta in the occupied West Bank when she was struck in the head by a bullet as Israeli settlers fired towards Palestinian houses, according to testimonies from residents. Several other Palestinians, including her son, were wounded by gunfire.

headlinePool.title: Australia sanctions individuals and company involved in illegal West Bank settlements
headlinePool.description: Foreign affairs minister Penny Wong says rapid expansion of settlements and settler violence are ‘extinguishing the possibility of a two-state solution’ The sanctions prohibit Australians and Australian businesses from trading with or providing financial or other support to three individuals and four organisations.
